conflicts: 4s 2P3/2 (74225.846 cm^-1): beam-foil lifetime 1.51(7) ns (Schectman et al. 1993) gives A(134.72 nm) = 5.64e+08 s^-1 and A(136.34 nm) = 9.78e+07 s^-1 (f = 0.153(11), 0.055(4)), about 35 per cent larger than the NIST ASD values 4.19e8 and 7.5e7 s^-1 (accuracy C+); the same paper lists earlier measurements f(1347) = 0.109(10) (Schwab & Anderson 1982), 0.10(3) (Clyne & Nip 1977), 0.113 (Lawrence 1967), 0.090 (Hofmann 1967).
4s 4P5/2 (71958.363 cm^-1): phase-shift lifetime 1.5 us +-15 per cent (Lawrence 1967) versus 4.3 us implied by the NIST ASD A = 2.3e5 s^-1 (accuracy D) of the 138.97 nm intercombination line.

2P1/2-2P3/2 interval: 882.3519(12) cm^-1 (Dagenais et al. 1976, isotope-weighted mean) versus 882.35283(23) (35Cl) / 882.35367(23) (37Cl) (Braun et al. 1982) versus NIST 882.3515; all agree within about 1 sigma of the older value. Isotope shift 37-35: +28.2(2.0) MHz (Dagenais) versus +25.2 MHz from the difference of Braun's two values.

notes: Literature search was limited: the session's web-search quota was exhausted, so sources were located through Crossref, HAL, OSTI, arXiv and NASA ADS queries and only open copies could be read (APS, IOP, Elsevier, Canadian Science Publishing full texts were not accessible). Hyperfine constants of the ground term are second-hand from Chichinin's JPCRD review (method 'compilation'). Signs: A, B as printed (Casimir convention, E = A*C/2 + B*[...]). The M1 A value is the calculated one adopted by NIST. Values marked 'derived' were computed here from the quoted measured numbers. Two-photon entries: wavelength_vac_nm is the laser wavelength (two photons of that wavelength reach the upper level).
